symptom: `change $a (A_B.Title = 'x')` — setting an attribute of the object reached through association `A_B` — passed `mxcli check` and `exec` reported "Created microflow", then failed the build with CE1613 "The selected association 'A_B.Title' no longer exists." at the change activity. Hand-patched-BSON probes proved the deeper fact: NO encoding of a through-association member is accepted by ChangeActionItem — `Attribute: Hop.A_B/Title` and `Hop.A.A_B.Title` are invalid AttributeIdentifiers (unloadable .mpr), `Attribute: Hop.A_B.Title` is CE1613, `Attribute: Hop.B.Title` is CE0226 (mxbuild checks the identifier against the CHANGED entity), so the form is unrepresentable, not mis-spelled
cause: Three layers disagreed. check: `checkMembers` (validate_member_refs.go) blanket-skipped every dotted member, trusting exec's FINDINGS #51 refusal to catch bad one-dot names. Writer: that refusal lives inside the `mod != nil` branch of `resolveMemberChange` — it fires only when the pre-dot segment IS a module whose domain model lacks the association. For `A_B.Title` the pre-dot segment is an ASSOCIATION name, `GetModuleByName("A_B")` misses, the guarded block is skipped, and `resolveMemberChangeFallback`'s one-dot heuristic ("1 dot => Module.Assoc") wrote `AssociationQualifiedName = "A_B.Title"` verbatim. The reader answers (nil, "module not found") for an absent module, so the real backend always took the skip path
file: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go (moduleExists + the one-dot refusal before the domain-model lookup), mdl/executor/validate_member_refs.go (backendRefusesModule; checkMembers reports the same shape), tests cmd_microflows_member_identifier_test.go + validate_member_refs_test.go; example mdl-examples/bug-tests/change-member-through-association.mdl
insight: **The trust boundary was drawn one branch too deep.** #51's refusal was real but conditional on the qualifier being a plausible module; check skipped dotted names citing a guard that silently did not apply to the Assoc.Attr shape. The decisive evidence was the probe matrix, not more code reading: six encodings hand-written into the stored BSON, every one rejected with a DIFFERENT error — that spread is what proves 'unrepresentable' rather than 'wrong spelling', and it kills the tempting fix of rewriting the member into some canonical form. To make the refusal fire on the real backend the existence question must go through the module ROSTER (ListModules), not GetModuleByName: the reader's not-found comes back as an error, so `err == nil && mod == nil` never fires in production — the first cut of this fix passed every unit test (mocks answered nil,nil) and still shipped CE1613 end to end. Existing writer mocks only answer GetModuleByName, so the two-tier lookup (name first, roster on error) keeps them honest without editing each one
